extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO/OED staff, and attorneys subject to USPTO discipline
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and sanctions governing professional conduct of practitioners before the USPTO, including communication, diligence, safekeeping of client funds, and reinstatement conditions following suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to inform client of correspondence received from the Office (37 C.F.R. §§10.23(a),(b) via 10.23(c)(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must inform a client of correspondence received from the Office; Respondent failed to communicate Notices to File Missing Parts, Office Actions, Notices of Abandonment, petitions, and revival information to the client in a timely and accurate manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in the Final Order: Notice to File Missing Parts (mailed Jan 22, 2010) and Office Action (Oct 25, 2011) were not communicated; Respondent did not inform client of abandonment, petition for revival, or revival until January 2013; Respondent misstated to client on July 23 and Oct 29, 2013 that there was 'no action' despite Office Actions having been received. Failure to convey dates and content of Office correspondence is cited as violative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neglecting a legal matter (37 C.F.R. §10.77(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must not neglect legal matters; neglect includes failing to respond to Office Actions, failing to pay required fees, and allowing applications to become abandoned without client knowledge or consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facts: failure to respond to Office Action caused abandonment; no fees were paid in the continuation application causing a Notice to File Missing Parts and eventual abandonment; failure to file trademark application despite client payment. Such omissions constituted neglect under the cited rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thoroughness and preparation (37 C.F.R. §11.101)
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall represent the client with the thoroughness and preparation reasonably necessary for the representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance drawn from the Order: inadequate preparation/thoroughness shown by filing errors (e.g., filing amendments that were non-compliant/elected another invention), preparing invoices with incorrect calculations, and failing to ensure that necessary fees were submitted. These failures support a finding of inadequate thoroughness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diligence (37 C.F.R. §11.103)
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall be diligent in representing a client, which includes timely prosecution and follow-up to prevent abandonment and to pursue client interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order examples: failure to timely respond to Office Actions, not paying fees, and not timely following up on Notices led to abandonment and loss of client rights. Diligence includes monitoring deadlines and acting to preserve client's applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication with a client (37 C.F.R. §11.104)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner shall communicate with a client as to the matter, including conveying important Office communications and the status of filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order cites failures to communicate Office Actions, Notices, petition and revival events, and inaccurate status reports (telling client there was 'no action' when there was). Proper communication requires conveying both substantive content and dates of Office correspondence, and informing clients of abandonments and remediation steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safekeeping client property and funds; accurate billing (37 C.F.R. §11.115)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must safeguard client funds/property and must prepare accurate fee calculations and invoices; overcharging or misallocating client funds violates the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific misconduct: invoice (Aug 5, 2010) showing improper charges ($770 for excess independent claims and $2,288 for total claims — overcharge about $3,058); billing for more claims than filed; accepting client payment but not remitting USPTO fees; charging for a trademark filing that was never filed. The Order notes restitution (goods provided) as mitigation for returning over-charged expenses and fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction for disciplinary proceedings (35 U.S.C. §§2(b)(2)(D) and 32; 37 C.F.R. §§11.19, 11.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director and OED have statutory and regulatory authority to bring and resolve disciplinary proceedings against registered practitioners under the cited statutes and regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order states jurisdiction explicitly as the basis for the proceeding and settlement approval; procedural posture and authority are governed by these statutes and regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreed suspension sanction (term and timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: The practitioner may be suspended from practice before the USPTO for a specified period as an agreed sanction; in this case, suspension for twelve (12) months commencing on date of Final Order approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order specifics: 12-month suspension; practitioner may seek reinstatement after nine (9) months, but remains suspended until OED Director grants reinstatement per 37 C.F.R. §11.60. Suspension applies to patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement prerequisites (exams, moral character, competency) (37 C.F.R. §11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conditions for reinstatement may include retaking and passing registration examinations and professional responsibility exams and demonstrating good moral character, competency, and learning in the law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order requirements: retake and pass the Examination for Registration to Practice in Patent Cases before the USPTO (per 37 C.F.R. §11.60(c)(1)); retake and pass the Multistate Professional Responsibility Examination with scaled score ≥85 and present results to OED; demonstrate good moral character and reputation, competency, and learning in the law as part of any petition for reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative and security requirements during suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative steps accompanying suspension include compliance with specific procedural provisions, dissociation from customer numbers and PKI certificates, and restrictions on applying for a Customer Number until reinstated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order specifics: Respondent shall comply with 37 C.F.R. §11.58 (duties upon suspension) and 37 C.F.R. §11.59 (duties of the Director); OED will promptly dissociate Respondent's name from all USPTO Customer Numbers and PKI certificates; Respondent shall not apply for or obtain a USPTO Customer Number until reinstated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice of disciplinary action
rubrics_metrics.description: Final Orders and suspension notices shall be published electronically and in the Official Gazette to provide public notice of disciplinary actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order requires electronic publication of the Final Order in OED's FOIA Reading Room and a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the provided Notice of Suspension text describing the violations and suspension terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigating factors considered (restitution and cooperation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Restitution to the client and cooperative attitude during investigation are mitigating factors that may influence the sanction imposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent made restitution by providing certain goods (including an automobile) to offset over-charged fees and stated he would not accept new clients pending conclusion of the investigation; OED noted cooperative attitude in mitigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of disciplinary record in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may consider the record of the disciplinary proceeding in future complaints or disciplinary matters as an aggravating factor or to rebut representations by the respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order states nothing prevents the Office from considering this record (including the Final Order) (1) when addressing further complaints or evidence of same/similar misconduct, and (2) in any future disciplinary proceeding as an aggravating factor or to rebut statements by respondent.
